lines.trans: Producer Ra Joon-mo's nickname is the jinxed prophet of the variety department.
Whenever he says his gut feeling is great it flops, and whenever he says it will fail it becomes a hit.
CEO, listen to me—never let this kid try acting or variety, just make him sing!
Everyone else is great except this girl has zero boldness or individuality—just debut them as a trio!
I really think you guys will make it big—this song is awesome and will launch a new Korean Wave!
At least he is consistent—always the exact opposite!
When music managers pick a title track, they purposely bring demos to Producer Ra to test them.
They drop whichever song he loves and make whichever song he says will flop their title track!
For a while now I have quietly suspected Senior Ra Joon-mo lacks a good sense for hits.
Please do not mention that I said anything like this.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

examples.text: 사람들이 연예인 이름 앞에 별명을 붙였는데 웃기더라고.
examples.trans: People put nicknames in front of celebrities' names, and it was really funny.

examples.text: 나도 그런 식의 별명이 생겼으면 좋겠다는 거지.
examples.trans: So I hope I get a nickname like that too.

meanings.note: Division of a television network that produces variety and entertainment shows.

examples.trans: He works in the variety department at a broadcasting station.
Variety department PDs are always busy.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 암튼 나 이번에 감이 무지 좋아!
examples.trans: Anyway, my gut feeling about this premiere is seriously great!
Here the word for 'gut feeling, intuition' is key.

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.
The exam went well.
I'm glad things worked out.

잘되다.gloss: to go well, to work out

meanings.en: to go well, to turn out well
meanings.note: 잘됐네 / 잘됐어요 = that's great / good for you
Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 술만 먹었다 하면 끊어지는 너의 망할 주사, 진짜 고마워 준모야!
examples.trans: Your wretched drinking habit of blacking out every time you touch alcohol—thank you so much, Joon-mo!
This expression comes from 'wretched, blasted'.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 감이 좋다 잘될 것 같다 그러면 망하고, 안 될 것 같다 그러면 잘되는 징크스가 있거든요.
examples.trans: Whenever he says his gut feeling is great it flops, and whenever he says it will fail it becomes a hit.
Here the word for 'a jinx' is key.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

meanings.note: verb listen

examples.trans: Listen well.
Listen to a song.
This is my friend Minsu.
He/she did it all.

meanings.note: Contraction of 이 아이; used when introducing or referring to someone younger or close
Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 대표님 내 말 들으시라니까, 얘는 연기 시키면 안 돼, 그냥 노래만 시켜!
examples.trans: CEO, listen to me—never let this kid try acting or variety, just make him sing!
Here the word for 'acting' is key.

meanings.en: to make someone do, to assign work
meanings.note: Causative verb; e.g., 일을 시키다 'to assign work'.
E.g., 치킨을 시키다 'to order fried chicken'.

examples.trans: The team leader assigned this work to me.
Shall we order pizza for dinner?

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.
Do you know any of my songs?
The topic of song came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.
Did you hear about this problem?
I was busy today because of problem.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 다 좋은데 얘가 문제네, 숫기도 없고 개성이 없어, 그냥 3인조 갑시다!
examples.trans: Everyone else is great except this girl has zero boldness or individuality—just debut them as a trio!
Here the word for 'even confidence' is key.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 다 좋은데 얘가 문제네, 숫기도 없고 개성이 없어, 그냥 3인조 갑시다!
examples.trans: Everyone else is great except this girl has zero boldness or individuality—just debut them as a trio!
Here the word for 'individuality' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 다 좋은데 얘가 문제네, 숫기도 없고 개성이 없어, 그냥 3인조 갑시다!
examples.trans: Everyone else is great except this girl has zero boldness or individuality—just debut them as a trio!
Here the word for 'three-member group' is key.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Colloquial spoken form of 너희네; used among close friends or to juniors.

examples.text: 너네 오늘 수업 몇 시에 끝나?
examples.trans: What time does your class end today?
You guys all come over here together.

meanings.note: Used before time nouns like 이번 주 (this week)

examples.trans: There is a meeting this Friday.
I will definitely succeed this time.

meanings.note: Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 나는 너네가 될 것 같아, 이번 노래 너무 좋고 한류의 시작이 될 것 같아!
examples.trans: I really think you guys will make it big—this song is awesome and will launch a new Korean Wave!
Here the word for 'of the Korean Wave' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 나는 너네가 될 것 같아, 이번 노래 너무 좋고 한류의 시작이 될 것 같아!
examples.trans: I really think you guys will make it big—this song is awesome and will launch a new Korean Wave!
Here the word for 'the beginning' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: At least he is consistent—always the exact opposite!
Here the word for 'as for consistency' is key.

examples.text: 난 원래 미소천사인데 반대로 가야지. 천년보살 신디 어때?
examples.trans: I am already a smiling angel, so we should go the opposite way. How about Saintly Cindy?
The topic of in the opposite way came up during this shoot.

examples.text: 노트북? 헤드폰? 다 필요 없어요. 차에선 무조건 잘 거예요.
examples.trans: A laptop? Headphones? You need none of those. You will sleep nonstop in the van.

examples.text: 무조건 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (without fail, unconditionally), we will get good results.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'manager'

examples.trans: The manager called.
Where is Cindy's manager?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 매니저들이 타이틀곡 뽑을 때 일부러 라 피디님한테 가서 듣게 하잖아요.
examples.trans: When music managers pick a title track, they purposely bring demos to Producer Ra to test them.
Here the word for 'title song' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 매니저들이 타이틀곡 뽑을 때 일부러 라 피디님한테 가서 듣게 하잖아요.
examples.trans: When music managers pick a title track, they purposely bring demos to Producer Ra to test them.
This expression comes from 'when choosing'.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.
I understand well (on purpose).
Today is a (on purpose) busy day.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Emphasizes necessity or strong intention.
Used with holding or closing actions.

examples.trans: Definitely contact me tomorrow.
Please close the door tightly.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 꼭 하라는 곡은 빼고 망한다고 빼라는 곡은 타이틀곡으로 하고!
examples.trans: They drop whichever song he loves and make whichever song he says will flop their title track!
Here the word for 'song' is key.

빼다.gloss: to take out; to remove; to exclude

meanings.en: to take out; to remove; to exclude
meanings.note: Used for removing someone from a schedule or taking something out.
Used in arithmetic.

examples.trans: Please take my name off the list.
I took the key out of my pocket.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.
I told you last time.
What did you do last weekend?

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
Used in spoken Korean dialogue (det).

examples.text: 얘 지금 살려고 발버둥 치는 거 안 보여? 이런 거 보면 인간이 진짜 제일 잔인해.
examples.trans: Do you not see it struggling to stay alive right now? Seeing things like this, humans really are the cruelest.
Here the word for 'this kind of' is key.

meanings.note: noun thought

examples.trans: Good idea.
Come to mind.

meanings.note: Contracted form of 이야기하다

examples.trans: Let's talk again later.
Please tell me honestly.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
